Replay

Steam packet transport

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Ownership and boundsValidation and outstanding work

Use the Steam Session backend to carry Replay packets through GodotSteam's SteamMultiplayerPeer. It uses the same typed handshake, seat admission, input/ action protocol, snapshots and checkpoint machinery as the other transports. The adapter retains a peer directly; it does not install SceneMultiplayer or rely on Kit. ENet shares its bounded packet/lifetime adapter.

The interface was checked against GodotSteam 4.22.1, upstream commit 5853a7741d174cfa37edee1ca44a11581a989d0b. The separately released GDExtension loaded under Godot 4.7.1 and exposed the expected native class/methods without initializing Steam. This is ABI/capability evidence, not successful Steam network delivery. The tested configurations are listed below.

Odin
runtime: transportgd.Steam_Runtime // stable address; outlives every using Session
if transportgd.steam_runtime_init(&runtime, MY_APP_ID) != .None {return}

options := rgd.SESSION_OPTIONS
options.role = .Host // .Client on the other device
options.backend = .Steam
options.steam = transportgd.STEAM_CONFIG
options.steam.runtime = &runtime
options.steam.virtual_port = 0
options.steam.host_steam_id = host_id // required for clients; u64, not a seat

err := rgd.session_open(&session, initial, model, options)
// Normal session_frame / session_changes / session_issue calls follow.

Initialization is explicit and uses the client Steam API. It can launch an app session/presence and requires a suitable installed GodotSteam build, Steam client and app entitlement. steam_available only checks native capability and has none of those initialization effects. Missing runtime/capability or an unexpected API shape returns a typed error; it does not silently fall back to ENet.

The runtime requests manual callbacks. Steam transport polling pumps run_callbacks before polling its peer. If the game is waiting for lobby/invite callbacks before opening a Session, call steam_runtime_poll in its own outer loop. Polling must remain on the Godot/Steam owning thread. This client-API adapter is not an implementation of the SteamGameServer SDK; .Server still means Replay's no-local-player authority role using the configured runtime.

Godot peer IDs and Steam IDs are different types/identities. steam_id returns the local Godot transport ID. steam_remote_id maps a currently connected peer to the Steam ID reported by the provider. steam_parse_id accepts nonzero decimal 64-bit IDs and rejects malformed/overflowing endpoints. A transport address is not a Replay simulation seat or a grant of authority; admission policy remains separate.

steam_open_peer accepts a fresh caller-created peer implementing the same API. The adapter validates the base class and required methods, retains the peer, attaches connection callbacks and calls create_host / create_client. Session options can supply that peer through steam.peer; it is borrowed only during open, then removed from the retained options. Normal operation constructs the native class dynamically. The supplied runtime must remain alive.

Ownership and bounds#

The shared MultiplayerPeer adapter keeps one owned 64 KiB receive buffer and a bounded connected-peer registry. A short destination preserves the pending packet until a later read can copy it. Reliable/unreliable modes are reported separately, channel zero is selected explicitly, and invalid targets/oversized outgoing messages are refused. The provider must support Replay's 64 KiB logical packet limit; GodotSteam's inspected Sockets implementation supports larger messages.

The wrapper forwards the shared adapter's connection generations. Pending copies and backend packets preceding a replacement connection cannot acquire the new peer generation. This local metadata does not authenticate a Steam ID.

Close all Sessions/peers before releasing their runtime. Callbacks are detached before peer shutdown, buffers and references are released, and repeated close is safe. steam_runtime_release clears the borrowed runtime binding; it intentionally does not shut down a Steam API shared with other peers or lobby services. Lobby membership, invitations and SDK shutdown remain application-owned lifecycle work. No invitation or message to another Steam account is sent by capability detection.

Validation and outstanding work#

tests/replay_steam/run.sh uses a named API-contract fixture: a Godot MultiplayerPeerExtension delegates packets to real ENet while exposing the inspected Steam constructor/mapping methods. Separate processes exchange 64 KiB payloads, exercise both transfer modes and pending-buffer copies, then run a complete Replay handshake, validated loot action and authority checkpoint. Constructor/initialization failure cases verify rejection and cleanup. The fixture uses no Valve service.

tests/replay_steam/capability_run.sh loads a supplied addon and inspects the real class/method surface with Steam auto-initialization disabled. The pinned release passed this on macOS ARM64. tests/replay_steam/live_run.sh is an opt-in live test for two logged-in Steam accounts/devices. Its output uses a separate live sentinel; contract or capability success cannot satisfy that gate.

Live Valve relay/P2P behavior, invitations/lobby UX, entitlement/account boundaries, SteamGameServer support and broader platforms remain pending. Room endpoint/recovery integration supplies explicit Steam addresses and fresh peer construction through takeover/rejoin. Its local contract fixture remains distinct from live multi-account acceptance. Existing ENet/RTC Room profiles remain available. These gaps stay requirements of the full roadmap; this adapter is not a completed Steam deployment.
